subject: medicine
title: Valvular and rheumatic heart disease

steps.tx: Picture rheumatic fusion of the commissures causing **mitral stenosis**, with breathlessness, orthopnoea, night dyspnoea and haemoptysis. Note atrial fibrillation with atrial clots that cause stroke. Feel a tapping undisplaced apex with a loud first sound, an opening snap and a rumbling diastolic murmur. Recall hoarseness from laryngeal compression in Ortner syndrome. Relieve pliable valves by balloon **valvotomy**, and prevent clots with **warfarin** in stenosis with fibrillation. Contrast soft first sound with displaced thrusting apex, pansystolic murmur to the axilla and third sound gallop of regurgitation, which worsens in pregnancy.
steps.say: Picture rheumatic fusion of the valve commissures, which is typical of a narrowed mitral orifice with obstructed flow. Note breathlessness with orthopnoea and night waking, which indicates rising pressure in the left atrium. Feel a tapping undisplaced apex with a loud first sound, which is typical of mitral stenosis. Listen for an opening snap with a rumbling diastolic murmur, which confirms turbulent flow across the valve. Note atrial fibrillation with atrial clots, which causes stroke without anticoagulation. Contrast regurgitation with a soft first sound and pansystolic murmur, which is heard through to the axilla.

steps.tx: The grayscale echo in diastole shows thickened doming leaflets with a **hockey stick** anterior leaflet and a restricted mitral orifice. The left atrium is severely dilated behind the **rheumatic valve**, reflecting chronic pressure overload from stenosis. Labels mark the aorta with anterior and posterior leaflets, ventricle and atrium for orientation. Doming with commissural fusion distinguishes rheumatic disease from calcific degeneration. Request Doppler gradients with pulmonary pressures after this view, and screen for atrial clots before **balloon valvotomy**.
steps.say: The grayscale echo in diastole shows thickened doming leaflets, which is typical of rheumatic mitral stenosis. The anterior leaflet forms a hockey stick shape, which results from fusion at the commissures. The orifice is visibly restricted, which causes the pressure gradient across the valve. The left atrium is severely dilated behind the valve, which results from chronic pressure overload. Labels mark the aorta with leaflets and chambers, which helps orientation in the examination. Screen for atrial clots after this view, which is essential before balloon valvotomy.

steps.tx: Picture calcific or bicuspid narrowing causing **aortic stenosis** with the triad of syncope, angina and dyspnoea. Feel a slow rising anacrotic pulse with narrow pressure, and hear a crescendo systolic murmur to the carotids with a fourth sound gallop. Offer transcatheter valves to high risk patients and root replacement by the **Bentall procedure**. Contrast collapsing water hammer pulse with wide pressure, early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge, and Austin Flint with pistol shot and Duroziez signs of **aortic regurgitation**. Suspect root dissection when tearing pain migrates.
steps.say: Picture calcific narrowing of the aortic valve, which is typical of outflow obstruction from the left ventricle. Note syncope with angina and dyspnoea, which is the classic triad of severe stenosis. Feel a slow rising pulse with narrow pressure, which is typical of significant obstruction. Listen for a crescendo systolic murmur to the carotids, which indicates turbulent ejection through the valve. Contrast a collapsing pulse with wide pressure, which suggests major regurgitation through the valve. Listen for an early diastolic murmur at the sternal edge, which confirms backward leak into the ventricle.

vis.alt: Aortic stenosis brings SAD with slow-rising pulse, narrow pressure and crescendo systolic murmur to the carotids; regurgitation brings collapsing pulse, wide pressure and early diastolic murmur with Austin Flint, pistol shot and Duroziez signs.
vis.caption: Narrow faints, leaky collapses.

steps.tx: Apply Jones major and minor criteria with fever for **rheumatic fever**, noting migratory arthritis with carditis, Sydenham chorea in girls, erythema marginatum and nodules. Prove recent streptococcal infection with rising antistreptolysin titres, and detect subclinical carditis with echo. Eradicate streptococci with penicillin, then prevent recurrence with long term benzathine **prophylaxis**. Warn that damaged valves seed endocarditis, so cover high risk procedures. Repeat sore throat injections for years into adulthood, since no **vaccine alternative** exists.
steps.say: Apply Jones major and minor criteria with fever, which remains the standard for rheumatic fever. Note migratory arthritis with carditis, which is the commonest major pairing in children. Watch for Sydenham chorea in girls, which appears months after the sore throat. Test antistreptolysin titres with echo, which confirms recent infection with silent carditis. Eradicate streptococci with penicillin promptly, which is vital to clear the triggering throat infection. Prevent recurrence with long term benzathine prophylaxis, which is essential for damaged valves for years.

steps.tx: Relieve pliable young mitral stenosis by balloon **valvotomy**, and repair prolapse with rings while replacing degenerate valves by tissue or mechanical prosthesis. Anticoagulate mechanical valves and fibrillation with warfarin by INR for life, since bioprosthetic valves degenerate without clicks. Prefer bioprosthetic valves when future **pregnancy** looms, because warfarin harms the foetus. Follow gradients with yearly echo, cover high risk dental work, diurese failure, and check lactate dehydrogenase for paravalvular **haemolysis**. Grade activity back through rehabilitation.
steps.say: Relieve pliable stenosis by balloon valvotomy, which is ideal for young valves without calcification. Repair prolapse with rings where possible, which is ideal to preserve the native valve without anticoagulation. Choose mechanical valves for young patients, which is durable for decades with lifelong warfarin. Prefer tissue valves when future pregnancy is planned, which prevents warfarin harm to the foetus. Follow gradients with yearly echo, which is vital to track deterioration before symptoms return. Cover high risk dental work with prophylaxis, which prevents endocarditis on damaged valves.
